findings.claim: The change only guards two diagnostic sites, and both sit inside `this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke(...)`. The generator does not report diagnostics (I believe it passes a null reporter; not checked). With a null reporter, `?.Invoke` never evaluates its arguments, so those two sites cannot have caused CS8785. The reporter named three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (735, 1009, 1101). The two fixed hunks match 1009 and 1101 (each offset by 27 lines). The third site, near old line ~708, has no hunk. It likely sits outside a `?.Invoke` and still throws when `GetObjectInfo` runs on a metadata `Item<int>`. If so, the generator still crashes and the app gets no resolver, so the requirement is not met.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ClosedGenericStructFromReferenceTests.GeneratorDoesNotThrowOnClosedGenericStructFromReferencedAssembly. It emits a lib containing `[MessagePackObject] public struct Item<T>` to an in-memory image, compiles an app whose `[MessagePackObject]` class has an `Item<int>` member, runs MessagePackGenerator through CSharpGeneratorDriver, and asserts that no generator result has an Exception and that sources were generated. It then runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer and asserts there is no AD0001.

findings.claim: The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of this compilation. Some of these are about a type declared in source. Example: a source `[MessagePackObject]` class derives from a metadata base class that is not a `[MessagePackObject]` type and has a public property without `[Key]`. MemberNeedsKey for that inherited member now gets location null (Location.None) and is silently discarded. Before the change the analyzer crashed. Now the source type compiles with no MsgPack004, and no other compilation reports it, because the base type is not a MessagePackObject. A better fix would fall back to the formatted type's identifier location rather than drop the diagnostic.

A confirming test would emit a lib with `public class Base { public int X { get; set; } }`, then compile `[MessagePackObject] public class D : Base { [Key(0)] public int Y { get; set; } }` against it and expect MsgPack004 on D.
